title: MIPI C-PHY trio (three wires, three levels): HS bursts with the 3444443 sync, 16-bit words as seven transition symbols, post-amble; the same trio decoded on the receive side

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Word to send; writing TX commits it. A burst starts with the first word and continues while words keep coming; it ends after a word with last set or when the next word is late

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Word decoded from the receive trio (one every seven clocks in a burst); reading RX frees it

fields.desc: write 1: clear the receiver's sticky error (ERROR stops being set)

irqs.name: TX_SENT
irqs.desc: a burst finished and the trio is back to idle

irqs.name: RX_DONE
irqs.desc: a received burst ended with the post-amble and a clean stop

irqs.name: ERROR
irqs.desc: the receiver saw a protocol error (entry not on +x, wrong sync, invalid wire state, missing transition, a symbol group above 65535, a stop inside a word or without post-amble, junk after it); sticky in the core, so the bit is set again on every clock until CMD.irq_clear

notes: t_a, t_b and t_c are the transmit trio and r_a, r_b and r_c the receive trio, 2 bits per wire (00 low, 01 mid, 10 high), one symbol per PCLK; they pass through unchanged.

A word takes seven clocks on the wires, so a burst of several words needs TX written and RX read at that rate: RX has one holding register and a word arriving while it is full is dropped (RX_OVF). The 16-bit to 7-symbol mapping is base 5, least significant digit first; it is not the MIPI mapping table.
